short: Made the emperor a symbol with no governmental power, and has never been amended since 1947.
full:
When the Japanese government's own revision committee produced a draft that barely altered the Meiji settlement, MacArthur's staff wrote a replacement in about a week in February 1946. Presented to the cabinet, translated, debated and amended by the Diet, it was promulgated on 3 November 1946 and came into force on 3 May 1947. Article 1 states that the emperor is the symbol of the state and of the unity of the people, deriving his position from the will of the people, with whom sovereign power resides.

His remaining functions are ceremonial and require cabinet advice and approval: appointing the prime minister designated by the Diet, promulgating laws, convoking the Diet. The peerage was abolished, the collateral imperial houses lost their status in 1947, and Article 9 renounced war and the maintenance of armed forces. Nearly eighty years on the text has not been amended once — no proposal has cleared the required two-thirds of both chambers — which makes it the oldest unamended constitution in force anywhere.
